After you add the source to your eventstream, you can publish it to stream the data into your eventstream. Using Eventstream with discrete sources to turn events into streams for more analysis. You can send the streams to different Fabric data destinations, like Lakehouse and KQL Database.

featureName: Eventstream Edit and Live modes
description: Eventstream offers two distinct modes, Edit and Live, to provide flexibility and control over the development process of your eventstream. If you create a new Eventstream with Enhanced Capabilities enabled, you can modify it in an Edit mode. Here, you can design stream processing operations for your data streams using a no-code editor. Once you complete the editing, you can publish your Eventstream and visualize how it starts streaming and processing data in Live mode.

featureName: Default and Derived Streams
description: Multiple streams are listed within the Real-Time Hub including Default and Derived streams. Default stream are automatically generated when a streaming source is added to Eventstream. Default stream captures raw event data directly from the source, ready for transformation or analysis. erived stream: A specialized stream that users can create as a destination within Eventstream. Derived stream can be created after a series of operations such as filtering and aggregating, and then it’s ready for further consumption or analysis by other users in the organization through the Real-Time Hub.

featureName: New streaming connectors for Kafka public clusters and more instances of SQL Server DB CDC
description: Additional connectors will be available through the Get Events experience, including Public Kafka clusters and SQL Server DB CDC.

featureName: Additional Fabric system events

featureName: Schema Registry in Eventstream Public Preview

featureName: Eventstream integration with Managed Private Endpoint
description: This integration with Managed Private Endpoints enables secure and private access to data sources behind a firewall or blocked from public internet access, allowing data to be streamed to Fabric Eventstream over outbound connections.

featureName: Eventhouse destination support Eventstreams
description: Eventstreams will add support for Eventhouse as a destination.

featureName: Set Alert on Real-Time Dashboards
description: In addition to monitoring Power BI and Eventstream data, Data Activator will support periodic querying against KQL queries saved in Real-Time Dashboards. These queries can be used to return exceptions, or track results over time to detect data changes or threshold conditions.

featureName: Enhanced trigger options
description: To represent the business conditions for monitoring, Data Activator will support more trigger conditions such as percentage changes over time, date/time functions, basic mathematic functions, signal absence detection and more.

featureName: Pro-Code support for CRUD for Functions/MV/Update policies
description: The new Pro-Code CRUD experience for Functions empowers developers to create, read, update, and delete Kusto Functions and Materialized Views through a streamlined, code-first interface. It eliminates the need to memorize command syntax, . This enhancement is designed to accelerate productivity while preserving full control for experienced users.

featureName: Eventhouse Minimum Capacity Adjustments
description: The "Min Consumption" button has evolved into two distinct features for greater clarity and control. Always On, now enabled by default, ensures continuous availability without incurring premium storage costs, while Minimum Consumption allows you to define a baseline compute level, optimizing for both performance and cost. This change enhances transparency and empowers smarter resource management.

featureName: Eventstream supports large message size
description: Currently the largest message size Eventstream can support is 1MB. This new feature will push this limit to bigger size to meet broader requirements.

featureName: Eventstream supports customers to upload own connector
description: This feature enables customers to develop or re-use their own Kafka connectors or open-source Kafka connectors on Fabric when there are no pre-built streaming connectors available.Personas* ISVs / Partners — Building connectors for their products to integrate with Fabric* Enterprise developers — Teams with proprietary or niche data sources not covered by built-in connectors* Data engineers — Needing to bring custom/legacy sources into real-time pipelines without waiting for first-party supportTop User Benefits* Bring any source — Connect to any data system with a standard Kafka Connect plugin, eliminating dependency on first-party connector availability* Zero infrastructure management — Fabric manages the Kafka Connect runtime, offset tracking, scaling, and monitoring* Familiar development model — Leverages the industry-standard Kafka Connect API; existing open-source connectors can be repackaged and uploaded directly* Opens the door to an RTI connector ecosystem — Enables customers, partners, and ISVs to contribute connectors, growing a community-driven catalog of sources beyond what the first-party team can deliver alone* AI-assisted creation — AI agents can scaffold and build connector plugins, dramatically reducing development timeHow It Helps OKRs* Connector coverage / source breadth — Unblocks the long tail of sources without engineering investment per connector* Platform stickiness / adoption — Customers invest in building on Fabric, deepening commitment to RTI* Partner ecosystem growth — Enables ISVs to create connectors, expanding the Fabric ecosystem* Time-to-value — Customers self-serve instead of waiting on the roadmap, accelerating onboarding**Competitive DifferentiatorManaged Kafka Connect as a platform primitive — Unlike competitors that require customers to stand up and operate their own Kafka Connect clusters, Fabric provides a fully managed runtime with built-in converters, offset management, and monitoring — all integrated into the Real-Time Hub discovery experience. Combined with AI-assisted plugin creation, this lowers the barrier from "weeks of infrastructure + development" to "hours with an AI agent and a ZIP upload."

featureName: Unify batch & streaming data platforms with CopyJob & Real-Time Intelligence

Fabric‑Native Data Access via OneLake - Customers can materialize governed master data in OneLake and use the data for both BI and AI use-cases2.Configurable Data Export & Synchronization - Ability to select specific master data, denormalize data, managaging update frequecy enabling self-service data provisioning which preserving the governance model in the MDM system3.AI enriched master data - Automated product description generation, intelligent data quality recommendations and corrections. 4. Unified Analytics via Power BI - Leveraging the full Power BI co-pilot capabilities.

featureName: Intuigence AI
description: Synthetic AI engineers for Industrial Operations that help users automate routine tasks so human engineers can bring their ingenuity to creative and complex challenges.Its industrial semantics, ontologies, physics aware models and purpose built agents supply the understanding that turns raw data into  industrial grade operational intelligence using RTI on Fabric as the backbone. Eventstreams capture and transform data at massive scale, eventhouse delivers fast and flexible analytics and OneLake ensures that context is unified and discoverable.

featureName: Spectral Core Workload Migration
description: Spectral Core delivers fast and worry-free migration solution, that makes it easy to move data, metadata and SQL transformations from populate databases and data warehouse to Microsoft Fabric.

featureName: Workspace level Private Link for SQL database
description: Private link allows customers to connect to their SQL DBs via a private endpoint from the customer’s virtual network. Workspace level private links will give customers the flexibility to use private link connection to specific workspace(s) which have high security requirements and contain sensitive data while their other workspace can be open to public.

featureName: Copilot for SQL Database in Fabric
description: New enhancements for Copilot for SQL database in Fabric include:* Improved response quality and consistency for Sidecar Chat / New toolsets to support scenarios like performance monitoring, troubleshooting errors, schema design, etc.

featureName: Editor for SQL database in Fabric
description: The SQL Query editor for SQL database in Fabric features include:* Datawarehouse & SQL feature parity (Bulk query delete, Keyboard shortcuts, Search bar filter, Code snippets, Column resizing) * Shortcuts* Shared Queries

featureName: Backup retention period
description: Backup retention policy is the capability to change the retention period which allows users to adjust the duration for which automated backups are maintained for a SQL database artifact. This feature directly affects point-in-time restore capability (specific period in which user can choose the specific point in time to restore their database to).

featureName: Fabric SQL - Restore of deleted databases
description: Users should be able to restore a database from backups of a deleted database in their workspaces.

featureName: Pre-/post-deployment scripts in CI/CD
description: The SQL database definition includes the objects that reside in the database, but the multi-dimensional nature of a database results in a requirement for additional actions during deployment. SQL database projects include a feature for incorporating open-ended T-SQL scripts for execution before and after the database deployment. Pre-deployment and post-deployment scripts unlock data cleaning before deployment, reference data management, and other advanced scenarios for CI/CD.

featureName: Fabric SQL DB in Workspace Monitoring
description: Integration on Fabric SQL DB in Workspace Monitoring.

featureName: Performance Dashboard in Fabric Enhancements
description: Multiple enhancements in Performance Dashboard including addition of memory are on the way.

featureName: Database create with all Azure SQLDB collations
description: Users will be permitted to set all supported collations in Azure SQL database for their SQL database in Fabric at the time of creation using REST API.https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/fundamentals/whats-new#sql-database-in-microsoft-fabrichttps://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/database/sql/deploy-rest-api?tabs=5dot1https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/fabric/sqldatabase/items/create-sql-database?tabs=HTTP#newsqldatabasecreationpayload

featureName: Mirroring Configurability
description: Ability to Start and Stop Mirroring/Replication using REST API'shttps://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/database/sql/start-stop-mirroring-api

featureName: Auditing for Fabric SQL DB
description: **SQL Audit for Fabric SQL Database**Auditing is an essential enterprise-ready feature and a critical requirement for SQL Database in Fabric. Default Auditing:auditing for Fabric SQL Database is designed to deliver security by default. This default auditing mechanism audits all activities, aligning with the standards of Azure SQL Database. It enables customers to meet compliance requirements for the Fabric SQL Database and ensures that all audit logs are written to a single lake target.Custom Auditing:custom auditing, allowing customers to configure auditing based on specific scenarios such as auditing data reads and writes, schema changes, or all activities. Customers will have the flexibility to select custom action groups tailored to their compliance needs. Additionally, they can configure retention policies and predicate expressions to achieve precise filtering of audit logs.

featureName: Database definition import/export API
description: Quickly export the database object definition (SQL project) via REST API, accessing the portable scripts of the database objects with the same tools as the rest of your Fabric objects. Update an existing database with a compiled database definition through the import object definition REST API, where any differences between the contents of the dacpac (compiled SQL project) and the existing database are calculated and automatically applied.

featureName: Shared queries in git integration
description: Track the contents of and changes to the shared queries in the Fabric git integration, creating visibility to how a query has been modified over time.

featureName: Git support for system object references
description: References to system objects (tables and views in the [sys] schema) can be validated during local development and in the Fabric source control integration.

featureName: Customer-managed keys (CMK) for encryption at rest
description: Encryption at rest using customer-managed keys, configured at the workspace-level.

featureName: Editor for SQL database in Fabric
description: The SQL query editor in the Microsoft Fabric portal is a powerful tool designed for writing and executing T-SQL queries. Here are its key features:* IntelliSense and Code Completion: Provides support for syntax highlighting, client-side parsing, and validation.* Query Execution: Allows running Data Definition Language (DDL), Data Manipulation Language (DML), and Data Control Language (DCL) statements.* Automatic Saving: Queries are saved automatically every few seconds.* Result Viewing: Displays query results in a grid, with options to search within results and download them in various formats (Excel, JSON, CSV).* Copilot Integration: Utilizes AI to assist in writing and managing queries, enhancing efficiency.* Keyboard Shortcuts: Offers various shortcuts to streamline query writing and execution.

featureName: SQL project database definition import/export API
description: The REST APIs for SQL database in Fabric are being extended to support the full SQL project file format in addition to the existing dacpac format. These APIs enable you to retrieve the code definition of your databases or have your database dynamically updated based on a code definition that you provide.- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/fabric/sqldatabase/items/get-sql-database-definition?tabs=HTTP- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/fabric/sqldatabase/items/update-sql-databases-definition?tabs=HTTPLearn more about SQL projects from https://aka.ms/sqlprojects

featureName: Git integration
description: A SQL Database in Microsoft Fabric has source control integration, or "git integration", allowing SQL users to can track the definitions of their database objects over time and across a team:* The team can commit the database to source control, which automatically converts the live database into code in the configured source control repository (Azure DevOps).* The team can update database objects from the contents of source control, which validates the code in Azure DevOps before applying a differential change to the database.

featureName: Deployment pipelines
description: Deploy database objects from one workspace to another with support for SQL in Fabric deployment pipelines. Per-object visibility to the differences between workspaces is available when comparing content between stages in the deployment pipeline.

featureName: OPENROWSET and Bulk support
description: Fabric SQL Database now supports OPENROWSET, and BULK INSERT operations for CSV, and Parquet file formats. Users can easily and safetly query and ingest files directly from OneLake.

featureName: SQL Backup billing
description: This release is for backup billing for SQL database in Fabric. We intend to start charging for this starting April 1st 2025.

featureName: Auditing for Fabric SQL DB
description: **SQL Audit for Fabric SQL Database**Auditing is an essential enterprise-ready feature and a critical requirement for SQL Database in Fabric. Default Auditing:auditing for Fabric SQL Database is designed to deliver security by default. This default auditing mechanism audits all activities, aligning with the standards of Azure SQL Database. It enables customers to meet compliance requirements for the Fabric SQL Database and ensures that all audit logs are written to a single lake target.Custom Auditing:custom auditing, allowing customers to configure auditing based on specific scenarios such as auditing data reads and writes, schema changes, or all activities. Customers will have the flexibility to select custom action groups tailored to their compliance needs. Additionally, they can configure retention policies and predicate expressions to achieve precise filtering of audit logs.

featureName: Scaled Configuration Canvas
description: The scaled canvas UX focuses on delivering a more consistent and scalable UX that supports advanced ontology configurations. Current workflows are fragmented and limit discoverability, making it harder for users to manage ontologies effectively. The scaled design features unified navigation, scalable and expandable elements, and better interaction patterns for clearer entities, relationships, rules, and more. This approach is grounded in user research, where participants responded positively to the navigation and ontology visualization, with feedback on specific pain points incorporated into iterative improvements.

featureName: Ontology Public Preview Release
description: A unified semantic layer that connects data points through meaning, not just structure, allowing systems and humans to interpret and act on data with context and consistency. The foundation for interoperability, intelligent automation, and AI explainability. A way to organize enterprise data into actionable intelligence.

featureName: Public API for Ontology
description: As a data analyst, I want to programmatically manage ontology schemas via a SDK  and query instances via API in so that I can automate and scale downstream analyses.

featureName: [Ontology for Copilot Studio] Ontology integration with CoPilot Studio
description: Fabric IQ Ontology serves as a first-class context source within Microsoft Copilot Studio, enabling you to build custom agents that understand your business domain out of the box. By connecting your ontology to Copilot Studio, your custom agents gain access to a structured semantic layer that defines your entity types, relationships, and business concepts — allowing them to reason over real operational data and deliver domain-aware responses without requiring custom prompt engineering or manual data wiring.

featureName: Fabric Planning
description: Planning in Microsoft Fabric is a native enterprise planning capability that brings budgeting, forecasting, and scenario modeling directly into your data platform—eliminating silos between planning, analytics, and AI.Built into Microsoft Fabric, Planning enables business and data teams to collaboratively create, manage, and refine plans on top of governed, real-time data—powering faster, more informed decision-making across the organization.

featureName: Fabric Graph delivers reliable performance at billion scale
description: Fabric Graph is designed to operate at very large scale, supporting graphs with billions of elements while maintaining predictable performance and reliability. Ongoing investments improve query stability, ingestion throughput, and service resiliency. Operational visibility is enhanced by exposing detailed ingestion failure information and clearer diagnostic signals, enabling customers to identify, understand, and resolve issues more quickly as graph workloads scale into production.

featureName: Fabric Graph enables fast insight with no/low code graph modelling, querying and exploration
description: Fabric Graph provides low code and no code experiences for modelling graphs, building queries, and exploring results. Customers can define graph models, manage reusable queries, and inspect outputs through UI driven workflows without requiring deep GQL expertise. These experiences lower the barrier to entry for analysts and application builders, while still allowing advanced users to drop down to full GQL for complex scenarios.

featureName: Fabric Graph makes connected data accessible through natural language data agents
description: Fabric Graph integrates with Fabric Data Agent and supports NL2GQL, enabling users to ask questions about graph data in natural language. Queries are translated into GQL, executed against the graph, and returned as grounded results. Users can inspect the executed query or navigate back to the graph experience for deeper exploration. This capability allows Fabric Graph to participate directly in agent driven and Copilot scenarios while maintaining transparency and trust.

featureName: Fabric Graph expands GQL support for real world relationship queries
description: Fabric Graph increases GQL feature coverage to support richer relationship modeling and investigation scenarios. This includes dynamic nested data, OPTIONAL MATCH, extended FOR semantics (IS SOURCE OF, IS DESTINATION OF, COLLECT ONE), result shaping functions (NODES, EDGES, INNER NODES), quantified simple edge patterns, and shortest path queries.

featureName: Fabric Graph enforces OneLake security for governed graph access
description: Fabric Graph conforms to OneLake security so that access controls defined over lake data are enforced consistently when data is represented and queried as a graph. Row , column , and object level policies apply end to end, preventing graphs from becoming an alternate access path. This alignment ensures customers can adopt Fabric Graph without introducing new security models or weakening existing governance and compliance controls.

featureName: Fabric Graph supports private network access for enterprise environments
description: Fabric Graph supports private connectivity using Fabric private endpoints and private links. This allows customers to access graph workloads over private networks, keep traffic off the public internet, and deploy Fabric Graph in locked down enterprise network environments. The service validates graph APIs under private access configurations and propagates the required access context for trusted service to service communication.

featureName: Outbound Access Protection for Fabric Graph
description: Fabric Graph complies with Fabric Workspace Outbound Access Protection (OAP). When OAP is enabled, graph workloads enforce outbound network policies, allowing connections only to approved destinations such as managed private endpoints. Non compliant outbound calls are blocked and surfaced clearly. This ensures Fabric Graph aligns with enterprise network security requirements and helps prevent unintended or unauthorized data exfiltration.

featureName: Fabric Graph – Generally Available
description: Fabric Graph is now Generally Available, delivering a secure, scalable, and enterprise-ready graph analytics capability powering Fabric IQ and natively integrated with Microsoft Fabric.Fabric Graph is engineered to operate at billion-scale, providing predictable performance, improved ingestion throughput, resilient query execution, and enhanced diagnostic visibility to support production-grade graph workloads. It expands GQL feature coverage to support advanced relationship modeling scenarios, including nested data, OPTIONAL MATCH, extended FOR semantics, result shaping functions, quantified edge patterns, and shortest-path queries.Fabric Graph lowers the barrier to graph adoption with no-code and low-code experiences for modeling, querying, and exploration, while still enabling full GQL control for advanced users. It also integrates in public preveiw with Fabric Data Agent and supports natural language to GQL (NL2GQL), allowing users to query connected data through conversational experiences while maintaining transparency through executable query inspection.From a governance and security standpoint, Fabric Graph will shortly enforce OneLake security policies end-to-end, including row-, column-, and object-level controls, ensuring consistent data governance without introducing alternate access paths. The service supports private network connectivity via Fabric private endpoints and private links, complies with Workspace Outbound Access Protection (OAP) to prevent unauthorized data exfiltration, and supports Realms for regional isolation in regulated and Microsoft first-party environments.With GA, Fabric Graph provides a fully integrated, secure, and scalable foundation for connected data analytics, operational workloads, and AI-driven agent scenarios within Microsoft Fabric.

featureName: Ontology Health
description: We are introducing Ontology Health in Microsoft Fabric to help modelers quickly assess whether an ontology is ready for real-world use. With this capability, ontology quality is continuously evaluated across three core areas—foundation, validation, and refinement—ensuring models are structurally sound, properly configured, and operationally ready. With this capability, you can: * Identify structural issues and inconsistencies through foundation checks to ensure the ontology is sound. * Verify required configurations using validation checks to confirm completeness and correctness. * Improve clarity, coverage, and usability with refinement checks for downstream consumption. * Quickly prioritize fixes with results categorized as Critical, Warning, or Information. * Navigate directly to impacted elements with guided actions, enabling faster issue resolution and increased trust in queries, graph experiences, and AI-powered outcomes.

featureName: Rules for Ontology
description: The rules feature of ontology (preview) lets you automate and manage event-driven alerts directly within your entity types. With the integrated capabilities of Fabric Activator, you can achieve real-time monitoring and response for your business entities. This feature allows you to define alerts that monitor properties across every instance of an entity type, to ensure comprehensive, ongoing oversight.Rules transform ontologies from static information models to dynamic and operational model. Now you are capable of automatically initiating business processes through alerts and automated actions, all within a seamless and context-aware environment. This feature helps you unlock automation capabilities without needing to switch between tools or write custom code, to streamline workflows and enhance efficiency

featureName: Resource Links - Link PBI Reports
description: Resource Links let you attach resources to the entity types they describe, so insights live alongside the data model that powers them. Starting with Power BI reports, when someone explores an entity in your ontology, they can immediately see the relevant Power BI reports that show how that data is analyzed, monitored, and used without needing to search across tools or guess which report applies.

featureName: [Ontology for Foundry IQ] - Ontology integration with Foundry IQ
description: Fabric IQ Ontology integrates with Azure AI Foundry to provide data scientists and AI builders with rich semantic context for training, grounding, and fine-tuning models and agents. By connecting ontology-defined business concepts, entity relationships, and domain vocabulary to your AI workflows, Foundry IQ enables more reliable agent behavior, improved reasoning over business processes, and better alignment between AI outputs and the real-world structure of your enterprise.

featureName: [Ontology for A365] - Ontology integration with Agent 365
description: Fabric IQ Ontology integrates natively with Microsoft 365 Copilot and Agent 365, providing AI agents with a rich semantic source of truth for reasoning over your business data. When users ask questions in natural language, agents leverage the ontology to understand the relationships between business entities, interpret intent consistently, and deliver grounded, accurate answers drawn directly from your enterprise data — all within the familiar Microsoft 365 experience.

featureName: [Ontology for Data Agent] - Ontology integration with Data Agent
description: Fabric IQ Ontology empowers the Data Agent to query and reason over your business data using natural language, grounded in a well-defined semantic model. Users can ask complex analytical questions and receive trustworthy, explainable answers with citations that trace back to the underlying ontology and data sources — giving teams confidence that insights are accurate, verifiable, and rooted in the true structure of their enterprise data.

featureName: Modeling Untyped Properties
description: This feature allows users to create property definitions without immediately selecting a data type or binding to a data source. Users can define high‑level business concepts first and assign data types later when real data is bound, at which point the entity type updates automatically. This flexibility lets users model concepts early without needing to know data types or source details upfront.

featureName: [Ontology MCP Endpoint] Query Tools
description: The Ontology MCP Endpoint provides a programmatic query surface that enables any AI agent or application to discover, explore, and reason over ontology data. Query tools support natural language search over ontology data, schema discovery through entity type and property listing, and structured entity/relationship traversal — giving developers and agents a single, consistent API to ask questions, retrieve answers, and build intelligent experiences grounded in your enterprise semantic layer.

featureName: [Ontology for Operational Agent] - Ontology integration with Operations Agent
description: Fabric IQ Ontology enables operational agents to reason over your live business environment using natural language, providing frontline teams with explainable, trustworthy answers backed by citations. Operational agents use the ontology as their semantic backbone to interpret questions about asset status, process state, and operational relationships — delivering grounded insights that help operators make faster, better-informed decisions without needing to navigate multiple data systems.
